{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-md-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"0feeb45c9174083fcaa24fa4510ad471ffcf1fd7ee1ce9fee3166c79830d6fff","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-md-class-c:lineage:38","source_registry_sha256":"fac6b4b22cda98085a5d7df11947d7cc05865e6c877c17be3df4d573863d1518","source_liveness_sha256":"43fe3511474bec2a914f5cdb112291b78f4339942c4d6fb903d9e3bae34bb3fc"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing the road (bicycles, mopeds, ADAS, confusables)","heading":"C2 — Bicycles, mopeds and scooters, and driver assistance technology, with sharing-the-road confusables","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Bicycles, mopeds and scooters, and driver assistance technology, with sharing-the-road confusables

FACT_ID: sec09-F34 | anchor: A39
Maryland law treats bicycles as vehicles; cyclists may use the road and must obey all traffic signals. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec09-F35 | anchor: A39
Cyclists are harder to see, quieter and unprotected by a vehicle body, so even a small driver mistake can seriously injure or kill one. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec09-F36 | anchor: A40
Expect cyclists on every kind of road except interstates and tolled bridges and tunnels, at intersections and circles, in any weather and at any hour. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec09-F37 | anchor: A40
Cyclists may ride in the travel lane for safety on narrow roads or to avoid hazards, and with no shoulder or with parked cars on the right the lane center is often safest. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec09-F38 | anchor: A40
In Maryland a cyclist may take the full lane even well below traffic speed when the lane is too narrow for a vehicle to pass the bicycle safely within it. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec09-F39 | anchor: A40
Check for cyclists coming from behind before you open a car door. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec09-F40 | anchor: A40
Cyclists have the right-of-way when a motor vehicle turns, and you must yield to cyclists in a bike lane or shoulder you enter or cross. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec09-F41 | anchor: A40
In a crosswalk a bicycle has the same right-of-way as a pedestrian, and failing to yield to a bicycle in a way that causes a crash brings fines and or prison time plus points. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec09-F42 | anchor: A40
Bicycles may ride on sidewalks statewide, yielding to pedestrians and mobility-device users, though local governments can ban sidewalk riding. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec09-F43 | anchor: A40
Slow down approaching a cyclist and do not honk, because a loud noise can startle the rider into a crash. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec09-F44 | anchor: A40
Cyclists use hand and arm signals since bicycles lack turn signals, and they may swerve or change speed suddenly to avoid holes or glass, so do not follow closely. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec09-F45 | anchor: A40
Pass a cyclist as you would any slow vehicle, waiting for oncoming traffic to clear and leaving at least 3 feet, whether the bike is in a bike lane, on the shoulder or in your lane. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec09-F46 | anchor: A40
After passing a cyclist, see the bicycle in your rear-view mirror before moving back into your lane. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec09-F47 | anchor: A41
Assume a cyclist is going straight through an intersection unless the rider signals a turn, and look both ways before crossing a sidewalk or trail. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec09-F48 | anchor: A41
Experienced cyclists can ride as fast as 35 mph and may be closer than they seem. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec09-F49 | anchor: A41
Never turn right from a through lane right after passing a bike on a shoulder or in a bike lane. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec09-F50 | anchor: A41
Before a right turn, check your right side and blind spot for bikes and move as far right as you can within the bike lane, shoulder or right turn lane. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec09-F51 | anchor: A41
Do not turn left directly in front of a bicycle, and look carefully for bikes before moving right to get around a left-turning vehicle. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec09-F52 | anchor: A41
Where a bridge, parked cars or another obstruction narrows the road, expect a shoulder cyclist to merge left into the travel lane. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec09-F53 | anchor: A41
At night a faint reflective object may be a bicycle in the travel lane, so use low beams as you approach a cyclist. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec09-F54 | anchor: A41
Young cyclists are the most likely to change direction without warning, so obey school-zone and residential limits to give yourself time around them. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec09-F55 | anchor: A41
Moped and scooter riders must follow all traffic laws, and their small size makes them hard for other drivers to see. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec09-F56 | anchor: A41
Mopeds and scooters may use any road posted at 50 mph or less, alone or side by side, on the road or shoulder, keeping as far right as is safe. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec09-F57 | anchor: A42
Advanced Driver Assistance Systems, or ADAS, are safety features that the manual says prevent 40% of crashes when used properly. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec09-F58 | anchor: A42
Examples of ADAS are Automatic Emergency Braking, Lane Keeping Assistance and Blind Spot Warning, which use sensors and cameras to spot dangers. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec09-F59 | anchor: A42
Do not rely on ADAS to drive for you; you stay responsible for safe operation and for checking traffic with mirrors and cameras at all times. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec09-F60 | anchor: A42
ADAS may not work properly in rain, snow, fog, on hills or around curves, and it behaves differently across vehicles with names that may not describe what it does. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec09-F61 | anchor: A42
Keep sensors clean and undamaged, keep the software updated, and learn each vehicle's systems from its manual or the dealer. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A38
Each truck no-zone has its own rule: beside a truck, make sure you can see the driver's face in the mirror; behind it, do not tailgate; in front, do not cut in until both headlights show in your mirror. [A38]
Why it matters: group_hint truck-no-zones; prereq_hint sec09-F17; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec09-F18, sec09-F20, sec09-F22.
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A37
For a moving emergency vehicle you pull to the edge and stop, but for a stopped one you move to a lane not next to it or slow and be ready to stop. [A37]
Why it matters: group_hint emergency-vehicles; prereq_hint sec09-F07; difficulty_hint 4; confusable_with sec09-F08, sec09-F10.
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A40
A turning driver must yield to cyclists, and in a crosswalk a cyclist gets the same right-of-way as a pedestrian, whereas a cyclist riding on a sidewalk must yield to pedestrians. [A40]
Why it matters: group_hint bicycle-right-of-way; prereq_hint sec09-F34; difficulty_hint 4; confusable_with sec09-F40, sec09-F41, sec09-F42.
